- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.13 to +0.37 in sentiment).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.37 to -0.50) or after a sharp drop.
- Model tends to overreact to recent highs, leading to overshoots in early forecast days (e.g., 1–3 days post-spike).
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts often fail to adjust downward quickly after a 70–75%+ price peak; true outcomes show stronger correction than model.
- Sentiment-driven lag: model reacts to sentiment shifts 1–2 days too late; if sentiment turns negative, forecast should drop 1–2 days before true drop.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early days (1–7) and underestimate late days (20–30), especially when sentiment is volatile.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is negative, don’t assume model is “correct” just because it’s trending; true outcomes often show stronger downside correction than model.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate; when sentiment is negative, model underestimates — use sentiment as a multiplier for adjustment (e.g., -0.15 to -0.25 for negative sentiment).
